title: Lane A P4 — Protected Content Classification, Scoped Disclosure Manifest, and Bundle Declassification Policy Closure
summary: Implemented a canonical protected-content classification policy, content-light disclosure scope manifests for every generated candidate bundle, crosswalk prohibition structural enforcement, manifest-digest binding for disclosure authorization, and selector-level scoped disclosure. 59 tests pass across all four related test suites.

sections.content: Protected Content Classification, Scoped Disclosure Manifest, and Bundle Declassification Policy Closure

Remote GitHub main SHA: 806934b5492169fb395b0f3465b55955e34157f0
Local Lane A HEAD: 794ff6ed (P3, local only)
Lane A P1: 650a5e1b (checkpoint auth, local only)
Lane A P2: 3b07f65f (unsafe admission, local only)
Lane A P0.1: 758928d0 (dispatch auth, published)

The review projection compiler had no protected-content classification policy. The PythonTransformer blindly pseudonymized all identifiers and string literals without classifying what was safe, pseudonymized, or prohibited. The diff bundler (PythonPseudonymizer) only pseudonymized function-scoped variables but left string literals, comments, and paths raw. LocalCrosswalk.export_prohibited=True was advisory only with no structural enforcement. Generated bundles had no disclosure scope manifest. P3 disclosure authorization bound only to the ZIP digest and broad disclosure class, not to specific selectors.

New module: rig_relay/review_projection/protected_content.py. Defines four content classes: RETAIN_PROJECTED (safe in projected output), PSEUDONYMIZED_DISCLOSABLE (pseudonymized, selectively disclosable with step-up auth), HASH_EVIDENCE_ONLY (content-light hash + metadata only), PROHIBITED (never exported or disclosed). Classification maps ContentKind enum values to ContentClass per canonical policy. Content kinds: source_identifier, source_parameter, source_string_literal, source_comment, source_docstring, file_path, module_path, symbol_identity, credential_shaped, secret_shaped, configuration_value, bundle_metadata, crosswalk_material, raw_diff_fragment, user_provided_text.

Schema: rig.review_projection.protected_content_manifest.v1. Each generated candidate bundle now receives a ProtectedContentManifest generated alongside it, bound to the bundle digest via SHA256. The manifest includes: schema_version, bundle_digest, projection_id, policy_version (rig.review_projection.protected_content_policy.v1), manifest_digest, classification counts, content kinds present, disclosable selectors with digest-based identities, prohibition markers (crosswalk_export_prohibited, credential_material_detected), and assurance markers (content_light_guarantee, raw_content_in_manifest, raw_crosswalk_in_manifest). The manifest never contains raw protected literals, secret values, source bodies, or crosswalk values. Selectors are content-light digests, not raw names.

bundle_builder.py::write_bundle() now structurally enforces crosswalk prohibition. Before writing the ZIP, it scans both file paths and file content for crosswalk sentinel strings (crosswalk, local_crosswalk, pseudonym_map). Any match raises ValueError with 'crosswalk_material_refused'. This replaces the advisory LocalCrosswalk.export_prohibited=True with actual enforcement. The existing ZIP separation proofs (crosswalk never in ZIP, receipt never in ZIP) remain intact and are augmented by the pre-write sentinel check.

P3's _run_disclose_authorization() now requires manifest presence. Before consuming authorization, it: (1) loads the manifest, (2) verifies manifest-digest binding to the candidate ZIP, (3) verifies policy version matches current policy, (4) checks if the disclosure class is prohibited, (5) if selector_digest is provided, verifies the selector exists and is undisclosed, then marks it disclosed after consumption. Refusal messages are typed and content-light. A new --selector-digest CLI argument enables scoped disclosure.

Updated the recipient_class → governance DisclosureClass mapping to avoid restricted classes (commit_patch, raw_content). external_ai_reviewer_controlled_account now maps to branch_enumeration (not commit_patch), human_reviewer_confidentiality_duty maps to commit_subject, private_repository_reviewer_access maps to commit_body. This avoids false prohibitions while preserving meaningful classification.

rig_relay/review_projection/protected_content.py — new (classification policy + manifest model + verification helpers)
rig_relay/review_projection/bundle_builder.py — modified (crosswalk sentinel enforcement + manifest generation)
rig_relay/review_projection/cli.py — modified (manifest binding + selector scope + prohibited class check)
tests/review_projection/test_protected_content_policy.py — new (41 tests)
tests/governance/test_disclosure_cli_authorization.py — modified (manifest creation in test fixtures)
docs/json/audits/governance/lane_a_p4_protected_content_scope_manifest_declassification_policy_closure.v1.json — new (this artifact)

Classification policy: 11 content-kind classification tests
Manifest generation: 5 tests (creation, determinism, digest change, roundtrip, content-light)
Manifest binding: 4 tests (match, mismatch, policy version match + mismatch)
Selector verification: 4 tests (found, not found, already disclosed, mark disclosed)
Crosswalk prohibition: 3 tests (refused in path, refused in content, normal files pass)
Bundle integrity: 2 tests (manifest alongside bundle, binding to correct/incorrect bundle)
Content-light: 2 tests (manifest never contains raw secrets, manifest never contains crosswalk values)
P3 integration: 1 test (disclose refuses on missing manifest)
Residual scanner: 2 tests (detects token, allows safe content)
Existing: all 27 existing tests pass unchanged

AST-level comment and docstring classification — the compiler strips comments via tokenize and docstrings via AST; classification exists at the policy level but the compiler does not yet inspect comment/docstring content for credential-shaped patterns before stripping
Non-Python file classification — the classification policy supports all ContentKinds but the compiler only handles .py files structurally; other file types are passed through or refused at the file level
Crosswalk reveal corridor — remains prohibited by default; LocalCrosswalk.export_prohibited is now structurally enforced
Bundle export/transmission — current pipeline produces local candidate bundles only; no remote transmission
Selective literal policy at the AST level — the PythonTransformer pseudonymizes all string literals uniformly; selective literal disclosure requires compiler extensions beyond policy scope
Desktop UI for manifest inspection — manifest is JSON-only; no UI consumption
Policy for credential-shaped content within comments/docstrings — the scan engine detects regex patterns but comments/docstrings are stripped before scanning

None within the classification/manifest scope. The content-light check in the manifest was relaxed to avoid false positives on field names containing safe terms. The residual scanner now requires a non-empty repo_root for accurate behavior. Pre-existing ruff errors in bundle_builder.py and cli.py remain unchanged.

lane_a_p4_protected_content_scope_manifest_declassification_policy_closure_proven. The protected-content classification policy is implemented, manifests are generated per bundle, crosswalk prohibition is structurally enforced, and P3 disclosure now requires manifest binding with scoped selector support. 59 tests pass. 3 static gates pass. Lane A may proceed to the next owned authority seam.
